evals.prompt: add a POST /orders/:id/refund endpoint to our express api (src/routes/orders.ts), it calls stripe and marks the order refunded in postgres. keep it simple
evals.expected_output: Reads package.json for versions first. Before writing, names the decisions that apply: owner/tenant authorization on the order, idempotency (a repeated refund request or client retry must not refund twice: idempotency key or a state check inside a transaction, plus Stripe's idempotency key), a timeout on the Stripe call with no blind retry, one error body shape, and no card or customer data in logs. Writes a contract-level test covering the double-refund and the unauthorized case.
assertions: Reads the project's versions (package.json or lockfile) before version-specific claims
Handles a repeated refund request so it cannot refund twice
Checks that the caller owns or may act on that order, not only that they are logged in
Sets a timeout on the Stripe call and does not retry it blindly
Plans a test for the double-refund or unauthorized case

evals.prompt: we need users.display_name to be required (NOT NULL) and drop the old users.nickname column, write the migration. app runs 3 instances behind a load balancer with rolling deploys
evals.expected_output: Does not ship NOT NULL and DROP in one migration. Splits into expand then contract: add display_name nullable or with a default, backfill from nickname, switch code to read display_name, enforce NOT NULL after the backfill, and drop nickname in a later release once no running instance reads it. Explains that old instances keep running during the rolling deploy.
assertions: Does not add NOT NULL and drop nickname in the same single migration
Backfills display_name before enforcing NOT NULL
Drops nickname only in a later step or release, after no running code reads it
Names the rolling deploy (old instances still running) as the reason
